newsitem.title: USA: Alaska lawmakers limit civil damage awards.
newsitem.headline: Alaska lawmakers limit civil damage awards.

text.p: Alaska legislators gave final approval Monday to a bill that limits awards from civil lawsuits and directs half of all punitive awards to the state treasury.
The House of Represenatives approved a version of the bill passed by the state Senate Friday.

The bill caps punitive damages at $500,000 or three times compensatory damages. In aggravated cases, the punitive award is capped at $7 million or four times the amount of financial gain that resulted from the defendant's misconduct, according to the bill.

It limits compensatory awards for non-economic damages to the greater of $400,000 or $8,000 per year of the plaintiff's life expectancy. In aggravated cases, the limit is $1 million or $25,000 per year of the plaintiff's life expectancy.

The final legislation was a compromise that resulted from negotiations between the Republican sponsor, Representative Brian Porter, and Gov. Tony Knowles and Attorney General Bruce Botelho, both Democrats.
Knowles last year vetoed a bill, sponsored by Porter, that would have limited punitive awards to $300,000 and earmarked 75 percent of punitive award recoveries to the state treasury.
A civil liability task force, appointed by Knowles after he vetoed last year's bill, found that most Alaska civil cases involved relatively small amounts of money and that punitive awards were rare.
